steps.say: When a teenager arrives in casualty unable to swallow even saliva because food is stuck, think beyond a simple blockage. In more than half of such emergency cases in older children, the real culprit is eosinophilic oesophagitis. These youngsters often have asthma or eczema in the background, and they tend to eat slowly or drink lots of water with meals. So arrange an endoscopy with biopsy instead of just clearing the bolus.
steps.tx: Seeing **food impaction presentation** in an adolescent should trigger thoughts of eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE, allergy driven food pipe inflammation). More than 50% of emergency presentations with acute food bolus impaction in older children and adolescents turn out to have EoE as the underlying cause. Ask about atopy (allergic tendency), asthma, eczema and slow eating, and arrange timely endoscopy (camera examination) with biopsy (tissue sampling) rather than repeated disimpaction alone.

points: Teenager with asthma, eczema or food allergy
Slow eating with heavy water drinking
left.title: EoE food impaction

steps.say: Inside the oesophagus, EoE leaves a very characteristic signature that you should recognise on sight. The scope may show stacked circular rings, vertical grooves running down the wall, and white specks of eosinophil clusters. The lining tears easily like wet tissue paper, and long standing disease narrows the lumen into strictures. The paired endoscopy and microscopy views here display exactly that combination of rings, furrows and dense eosinophil infiltration.
steps.tx: The **endoscopic visual findings** of eosinophilic oesophagitis are distinctive once you know them. Circular rings called trachealization (stacked fixed folds) or felinization (fine transient folds), linear longitudinal furrows (vertical grooves), white plaques or exudates (eosinophil clusters), mucosal fragility termed crepe-paper oesophagus (tears on scope contact), and strictures (fibrotic narrowing) make up the classic picture. Rings plus furrows together are highly suggestive, and strictures signal chronic fibrostenotic disease needing dilation.

vis.alt: Endoscopic rings, linear furrows and whitish exudates, beside a mucosa packed with eosinophils.
vis.caption: Endoscopic and histologic pattern of eosinophilic esophagitis. StewardMD original.

steps.say: A red oesophagus alone never proves EoE, so the microscope has the final word. The pathologist scans every biopsy at high magnification and records the densest hotspot, not an average. Only when that peak count reaches the accepted cutoff, and mimics such as reflux or infection are excluded, can you stamp the diagnosis. The same paired figure reminds you that endoscopy and histology must agree before treatment starts.
steps.tx: The **histological diagnostic threshold** demands at least 15 eosinophils per high power field (HPF, the view at 400 times magnification) on oesophageal mucosal biopsy, counted at the densest hotspot (peak count at x400 magnification). Counts below this cutoff, or eosinophilia explained by secondary causes such as reflux disease, infection, Crohn disease or coeliac disease, do not qualify. Insist on the peak eosinophil number in every pathology report, because treatment and follow up hinge on it.

nodes.label: Atopic child with dysphagia or impaction
Endoscopy shows rings, furrows or plaques

steps.say: EoE never spreads evenly, so one pinch from the bottom proves nothing. Take at least six pinches, split between the upper and middle gullet and the lower end, including a bite from normal looking lining. That two level approach pushes detection above ninety five percent. A lone distal sample will miss disease sitting higher up, so label every jar with its exact site.
steps.tx: The **multiple biopsy requirement** exists because eosinophilic infiltration is patchy (unevenly distributed). Take at least 6 mucosal biopsies from both the proximal and mid oesophagus and the distal oesophagus, targeting rings, furrows and normal areas alike. This two level sampling lifts diagnostic sensitivity above 95-97%, while a single distal biopsy misses disease hiding higher up. Document the site of each jar so the peak count can be mapped.

rows: Catches patchy disease hiding higher up
Hotspots can hide in normal mucosa

steps.say: Do not skip the PPI step just because the scope screams EoE. Reflux frequently rides along, and high dose omeprazole calms both the acid and the allergy signal that recruits eosinophils. Treat for eight to twelve weeks, then scope again. Roughly a third to a half of children remit on this alone. Those who respond simply stay on the PPI, while the rest move on to swallowed steroids or diet therapy.
steps.tx: A **proton pump inhibitor trial** comes first even when EoE looks certain, because acid and allergy often coexist. Give high dose omeprazole at 1-2 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 8-12 weeks, then repeat endoscopy with biopsy. About 30-50% of patients reach histological remission through acid blockade plus a direct anti-eotaxin-3 effect (calming the signal that summons eosinophils). Responders continue the PPI; non-responders step up to topical steroids or diet.

vis.alt: Cutaway of the lower oesophagus and stomach. Labels mark the oesophageal sphincter, a hiatus hernia, acid reflux, mucosal erosion on the oesophagus and in the stomach, Barrett metaplasia, and the gastric fundus.
vis.caption: Conclusive reflux disease includes the mucosal injury drawn here, with Barrett metaplasia above the junction. Illustration: StewardMD.

steps.say: Steroids help most when they touch the gullet rather than the airways. Mix budesonide into a thick slurry, or puff fluticasone into the mouth and gulp it down, so the drug slides slowly over the lining. Younger children need one milligram and older ones need two. Give it at bedtime after brushing, allow nothing by mouth for half an hour, and check the tongue for thrush at review.
steps.tx: When PPI treatment fails, **swallowed topical steroids** coat the oesophagus instead of the lungs. Use viscous budesonide slurry (thick liquid steroid) at 1 mg daily for children below 10 yr of age, rising to 2 mg daily at 10 yr and above; alternatively spray fluticasone from an inhaler into the mouth and swallow it. Take the dose after brushing teeth at night, avoid eating or drinking for 30 minutes, and watch for oral candidiasis (mouth thrush).

rows: 1 mg below 10 yr, 2 mg at 10 yr and above
Swallow slowly, nil by mouth 30 minutes
No spacer, no rinsing for 30 minutes

steps.say: Elimination diet sounds harsh, yet it frees most children from daily drugs. Cut out milk, wheat, egg, soy, nuts and seafood completely for two to three months under a dietitian, watching growth closely. Then bring foods back one at a time, scoping between steps to catch the true culprits. More than seventy percent remit, and many end up avoiding only one or two foods for good.
steps.tx: The **six-food elimination diet** removes the commonest triggers empirically (without prior testing). Exclude cow milk, wheat, egg, soy, peanuts and tree nuts, and fish and shellfish for 8-12 weeks with dietitian supervision (expert meal planning), then reintroduce foods one by one with endoscopic checks. Over 70% of children reach clinical and histological remission, and most families prefer diet over chronic drugs once a smaller set of true triggers emerges.

steps.say: When steroids and diet both fail, dupilumab offers a precise strike at the root signal. It locks the shared receptor for the two key allergy messengers, interleukin four and thirteen, starving the oesophagus of fresh eosinophils. From one year of age and fifteen kilos upward, a small injection under the skin every fortnight changes the game. Warn families about itchy eyes and sore injection spots.
steps.tx: For severe refractory disease, **dupilumab biologic therapy** blocks the allergy signal itself. This monoclonal antibody (laboratory made targeted protein) binds interleukin-4 receptor alpha (IL-4R-alpha, the shared docking site), shutting down both interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling (the messengers driving eosinophil recruitment). It is approved from 1 year of age in children weighing at least 15 kg, given by subcutaneous injection (under the skin), with conjunctivitis and injection site reactions as watchpoints.

points: From 1 year of age, weight 15 kg or more
Injection with eye checks at review

points: Local thrush and adrenal caution with chronic use
